name: sexual health overview
title: Approach to a sexual health concern: know your biases, ask permission and take the CDC 5 P's, then the Pleasure questions place the concern in a phase of the response cycle (desire, arousal, orgasm and resolution) or outside it (pain, illness, trauma); each column gives the question to ask, what is normal in both sexes, and how women and men differ

nodes.title: A sexual health concern: take the history, then find the PHASE it affects
lines: STEP ONE: know your own implicit biases before you walk in · stay NONJUDGMENTAL, whatever they admit to
ask PERMISSION, proactively · confidentiality early · open questions, silence, REPETITION to unpack a euphemism ("I think I need a check up")
CDC 5 P's: Partners · Practices · Protection + Past sexually transmitted infections · Pregnancy plans · ± Pleasure

nodes.title: A PHASE of the response cycle: the PLEASURE questions find it
lines: Masters + Johnson: excitement → plateau → orgasm → resolution · Kaplan: sexual drive → excitement → orgasm

nodes.title: NOT a phase
lines: pain is one of the Pleasure questions

nodes.title: Desire
lines: Kaplan put it first

nodes.title: Arousal
lines: excitement + plateau

nodes.title: Interest in sex, or a lack of it?
lines: "Any change in your (or your partner's) desire, or how often you have sex?"

nodes.title: Difficulty with lubrication? Getting or keeping an erection?
lines: erectile dysfunction: one of the two commonest concerns in men

nodes.title: Difficulty reaching orgasm? With ejaculation?
lines: premature ejaculation: the other commonest concern in men

nodes.title: Pain with intercourse? An illness?
lines: "Many people are concerned about how this condition might affect their sex life. What is your experience?"

nodes.title: Neurotransmitters + hormones set it
lines: • PRO-sexual: dopamine, noradrenalin, oxytocin, melanocortin
• INHIBITORY: prolactin, serotonin at 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) 2 + 3 receptors, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)

nodes.title: Vasocongestion
lines: • nitric oxide (NO): the major neurotransmitter of clitoral engorgement
• ↑ muscle tension (myotonia), heart rate, blood pressure

nodes.title: A CEREBRAL event
lines: • still possible after a COMPLETE spinal cord injury
• contractions every 0.8 seconds

nodes.title: Their answer decides what you offer
lines: information on the illness and sexual function

nodes.title: Women: desire need not come FIRST
lines: most widely used model (Basson), a circle: arousal can TRIGGER desire

nodes.title: What turns women and men on differs
lines: cultural expectations play a large role

nodes.title: Women: genital ≠ subjective arousal
lines: • NOT necessarily concordant
• seeing or feeling their own arousal matters less

nodes.title: Men: penile erection
lines: • testes elevate
• scrotum contracts

nodes.title: Women: NO refractory period
lines: → multiple orgasms possible

nodes.title: Men: a REFRACTORY period
lines: no other orgasm or ejaculation possible during it

nodes.title: Women also raise
lines: • dyspareunia (painful sex)
• body image
• unmet needs
• abuse or coercion

nodes.title: Men: especially likely to feel ashamed
lines: allow time: 45–60 minutes is ideal, or book a LONGER visit

panels.title: Make the office a safe space
items: gender identity, pronouns and sexual preference as ROUTINE intake-form questions
two-step method: ask gender identity AND sex assigned at birth
staff trained in culturally sensitive terms · gender-inclusive forms · diverse images
adverse childhood experiences (sexual abuse, trauma) can make the topic hard to discuss
